subject: Reactive functions as a data source

messages.author: 3e06428f200265c8
messages.subject: Reactive functions as a data source
parts:
Hi,

I'm using shiny with RMySQL to provide a frontend for some data we capture.  I have a reactive function and a few plots like:

getSomeData <- reactive({
  # do a MySQL query based on some input parameters
})


output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
  ggplot(getSomeData() ...
})

output$plot2 <- renderPlot({
  ggplot(getSomeData() ...
})

 Does it query the database for each plot or just once?  If I understand the Reactive conductors portion of the tutorial correctly, it would only be once.

Also, does that mean I can hook up another reactive function to getSomeData() and still only have 1 mysql call?  

procSomeData <- reactive({
  getSomeData()
})

Thanks.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Reactive functions as a data source
parts: It executes just once. And yes, in the procSomeData case there would still be just one MySQL call. (Until the inputs change, of course)

messages.subject: Re: Reactive functions as a data source
parts:
I'm trying to do the same, using a mysql query as input:

But when i do:

datasetInput <- reactive({
  datos.online <- fetch(dbSendQuery(datos, "select * from prueba2"), n=-1)
 
  #datos.online$Peso[datos.online$Peso < -10000] = NA
})

And them:

output$TempPlot <- renderPlot({
    plot.ts(datasetInput[,5:7], plot.type=c("single"), col=rainbow(3), main="sensores de temperatura")
    })

in server.R, i'm getting and error. something like: Error: Objetc of type 'closure' isn't a subconjunt (objeto de tipo 'closure' no es subconjunto, translated from spanish)


Do you have any tips?


Regards,

El martes, 14 de mayo de 2013 04:48:52 UTC-3, Joe Cheng [RStudio] escribió:
It executes just once. And yes, in the procSomeData case there would still be just one MySQL call. (Until the inputs change, of course)
